about: What each proforma line shows in each column. The phone renders a PDF (app/lib/pdf/proforma_pdf.dart) and the dashboard renders HTML (client/src/features/orders/ProformaDocument.tsx); both are the same document to a customer, so both read this file in their tests.

removed.item_code: an internal code the customer has no use for
removed.hsn: and the HSN summary table with it
removed.gst: the GST% column, the CGST/SGST/IGST breakup and the tax total - a proforma here quotes a price, and the tax is settled on the invoice
removed.per: replaced by the unit printed under MRP

packing_moved_out_of_description: Rolls, belts and cans were printed as a second line under the item name. They are quantities, so they are columns.
reconciles: Every row must multiply out against a column the customer can see. PCTR, CTR and BG are billed by weight, so Qty(kg) x MRP = Amount. VS is billed by the can, so Cans x MRP = Amount - which is why MRP carries its unit underneath.

lines.why: precured tread rubber shows rolls AND belts, and is billed by weight at a per-kilogram MRP
loose belts are shown when there are any - a customer who ordered 4 rolls and 2 belts must see both
hot rubber has rolls but never loose belts - it is not cut into them, so the belts cell stays empty rather than printing a zero
vulcanising solution is counted in cans and billed by the can - the tin size is already in the item name, so the can COUNT is what the column carries

the solution row must MULTIPLY OUT: the PDF used to print qty 90 against rate 195 and an amount of 585, which is three different numbers that do not reconcile. Cans x MRP is what agrees with the amount
bonding gum is sold by the kilogram and needs no packing column at all
a zero never prints - an empty cell reads as 'not applicable', a 0 reads as 'none supplied', and on a packing column those are different claims
an order raised before the per-kilogram rate existed falls back to the stored qty and rate, so an old proforma still reprints correctly
